title: Veterans' Compensation Cost-of-Living Adjustment Act of 2017
official_summary:
(This measure has not been amended since it was reported to the House on May 19, 2017. The summary of that version is repeated here.)

Veterans' Compensation Cost-of-Living Adjustment Act of 2017

(Sec. 2) This bill directs the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) to increase, as of December 1, 2017, the rates of veterans' wartime disability compensation, additional compensation for dependents, the clothing allowance for certain disabled veterans, and dependency and indemnity compensation for surviving spouses and children.

Each such increase shall be the same percentage as the increase in benefits provided under title II (Old Age, Survivors and Disability Insurance) of the Social Security Act, on the same effective date.

The VA may adjust administratively, consistent with such increases, the rates of disability compensation payable to persons entitled to veterans benefits under public laws administered by the VA on December 31, 1958, who have not received benefits under provisions governing veterans compensation for service-connected disability or death.

(Sec. 3) The VA shall publish such increased rates in the Federal Register not later than the date on which certain social security increases are required to be published in FY2018.

summary.headline: This 2017 law requires the VA to raise certain veterans' and survivors' benefits by the same percentage as Social Security benefits, starting December 1, 2017.
summary.what_it_does: The law directs the Department of Veterans Affairs to increase several monthly payments on December 1, 2017. The increases cover wartime disability compensation, extra pay for dependents, the clothing allowance for some disabled veterans, and dependency and indemnity compensation for surviving spouses and children. Each increase is the same percentage as the Social Security benefit increase taking effect on the same date. The law also requires the VA to publish the new rates in the Federal Register.

who_it_affects.how: Their monthly disability payments rise by the same percentage as Social Security benefits.

who_it_affects.group: Veterans with dependents who receive additional compensation for those dependents
who_it_affects.how: The extra amount paid for each dependent rises by the same Social Security percentage.

who_it_affects.group: Disabled veterans who receive the clothing allowance
who_it_affects.how: The clothing allowance rises by the same Social Security percentage.

who_it_affects.group: Surviving spouses and children receiving dependency and indemnity compensation
who_it_affects.how: Their monthly survivor payments rise by the same Social Security percentage.

who_it_affects.group: Certain veterans under pre-1958 benefit laws who have not received service-connected compensation
who_it_affects.how: The VA may adjust their disability compensation rates to match the same increase.

summary.when_it_takes_effect: The increased rates take effect December 1, 2017.
